findings.title: Live third-party API key hard-coded in client-side code ships to every browser.
User-written review body and third-party translation rendered as raw HTML (stored XSS).
Authors fetched one request per review, sequentially in a loop (N+1 waterfall).
Effect ignores productId changes and never aborts, so stale or out-of-order reviews are shown and state is set after unmount.
Floating load() promise: any fetch or JSON failure is unhandled and leaves the component stuck on the loading state with no error UI.
Response status is never checked before parsing; error bodies are treated as review lists.
API response cast to Review[] with no runtime validation.
productId (and authorId at line 55) interpolated into URL paths without encodeURIComponent, allowing path manipulation.
Translate control is a clickable div: not focusable or keyboard operable and has no button role.
Debug console.log left in, dumping all review and author data to the console.
Cached translation keyed only by review id, so a changed targetLanguage keeps showing the old language.
Translation error swallowed and the error message replaces the review body instead of a separate alert; error is not logged.
Third-party translation response cast without validation before being injected into the DOM.
findings.evidence: const data = (await res.json()) as { translation: string };

findings.title: useMemo is imported but never used.
deleteTask server action deletes any task by id with no session or project-membership check (broken access control).
findings.evidence: const { projectId } = await db.task.delete({ where: { id }, select: { projectId: true } });

findings.title: Module-level server QueryClient is shared across requests, so dehydrate() serializes other users' and other projects' tasks into each page.
findings.evidence: const serverQueryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 60_000 } } });

findings.title: One module mixes server-only code (db, logger, next/cache, inline 'use server' actions) with hook-using client components and has no 'use client' boundary; it either fails in RSC or bundles server code for the client.
Array index used as key for stateful TaskCards; after a task moves, local state such as confirmingDelete attaches to a different task, so the wrong task can be deleted.
`length &&` renders a literal 0 in every empty column.
Optimistic status update has no rollback and refetches only on success, so a failed move stays shown as saved.
Search fires a request per keystroke with no abort or ignore flag, so out-of-order responses overwrite newer results (race), with no debounce.
Interval effect has empty deps but reads updatedAt, so the label keeps the stale timestamp after the task changes.
Initial label depends on Date.now() during server render, causing hydration text mismatches.
Task is looked up before the membership check, so non-members can tell existing task ids from missing ones by the error.
findings.evidence: const { projectId } = await db.task.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id }, select: { projectId: true } });
